notes:
Company: ByteWing DevTools - VS Code-first copilots startup.

Summary:
- Building an opinionated VS Code extension that surfaces streaming completions and inline suggestions with real-time token diffs to the active editor.
- Primary ask: low-latency streaming (aim: 20-80ms per token avg) and stable version pinning for models per customer plan.
- Want hosted API for speed of integration but need optional VPC for enterprise customers.

Key requirements / acceptance criteria:
- Streaming completion: server->client chunked deltas, resume on reconnect, per-user session context preserved.
- Inline suggestions: sub-100ms median suggestion latency for single-line completions, predictor warmed via KV cache.
- Auth: support both org SSO (OAuth/OIDC) for billing accounts and per-developer API keys for dev preview.
- Rate limits: fine-grained per-developer quotas, burst behavior, and token-level billing attribution to customers.
- Model/version pinning: ability to pin stable model variants for canary and prod channels; automated fallback to smaller quantized model when capacity constrained.
- Observability: token-level cost reporting and error traces tied to extension telemetry.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (AE Jordan R., SE Liam C.), demo of Redwood streaming API prototype.
- 2026-01-28: Sent integration checklist + security FAQ (drive links above).
- 2026-02-11: Deep-dive session (Fireflies ff_2026-02-11_0b7c9a) re: streaming vs chunked websocket.
- 2026-02-18: ByteWing delivered sample extension telemetry (logs attached to INF-8921).
- 2026-02-25: Legal requested data residency clause; Redwood legal working with ByteWing counsel.
- 2026-03-03: SE run: local load test showed median latency 110ms; target <80ms for inline suggestions.
- 2026-03-08: Agreed on 2-week POC scope: embed Redwood client, simulate 100 concurrent dev sessions, validate model pinning and fallback logic.

POC scope / milestones:
- Week 1: Integrate streaming SDK inside extension background process; test reconnect/resume behavior.
- Week 2: Run synthetic load test (100 concurrent sessions) and collect token-level cost/latency metrics; iterate on batching and cache TTLs.
- Eval criteria: median suggestion latency <80ms, graceful fallback to smaller model without errors, audit logs available for session playback.

Notes from calls / direct quotes:
- "We need the inline suggestion UX to feel like a native editor — latency is make-or-break." — Lead PM (ByteWing).
- "Per-developer quotas + burst control must be configurable from the console." — CTO (ByteWing).

Technical concerns / follow-ups for Redwood:
- Confirm websocket vs SSE support for streaming SDK in constrained environments (corporate proxies).
- Provide example token-billing mapping for streaming sessions (sample invoice math).
- Suggest default batching/caching profiles for short-turn completion workloads (IDE traffic).
- Clarify SSO mapping model: organization billing account vs per-developer identity.

Commercial notes:
- Upside: ByteWing has multiple enterprise prospects; if POC succeeds, potential Dedicated contract as part of enterprise bundle.
- Pricing sensitivity: wants predictable per-seat pricing with soft caps rather than unbounded token bills.

Next actions (short):
- SE (Liam) to push SDK branch and sample extension by 2026-03-12.
- Jordan to coordinate legal with Redwood contracts on residency clause; target resolution 2026-03-20.
- Run first 100-dev load test and share results in INF-8999.

Misc: They mentioned competitor experiments with TabNine + custom LLM; interested in Redwood's quantized fallback to reduce cost.
